pins.name: AREF
pins.note: A reference, not a rail. It sets a converter's full scale and is not a supply the part draws from.

pins.name: ~{RESET}
pins.note: Reset must be strapped or driven. A floating reset is the classic intermittent-boot fault.

companions.rationale: Each supply pin needs a local ceramic to supply the switching current the rail cannot deliver fast enough; without it the die sees its own supply collapse on every edge.
One bulk capacitor per device holds the rail up through load steps the decoupling caps are too small for.
A capacitor on reset stretches the release past the supply's rise and keeps noise off the pin.
AVR reset is active low with only a weak internal pull-up, and the ISP header drives it. An external pull-up is expected.
AREF is a reference output when the internal reference is selected; the capacitor is what makes it quiet enough to convert against.

rules.rationale: A supply or return pin that reaches no net means the part is unpowered.
A floating input sits at an undefined level and picks up whatever is nearby.
Pins the symbol groups into one domain landing on different nets is usually a wiring slip, occasionally deliberate.
One crystal pin wired and the other not means the oscillator was half-connected; internal-RC designs connect neither.
